inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted = basic; constant 32,694,632 shares FY2016-FY2026, no options/SBC scheme, confirmed in FY2026 annual report EPS note (line 1271-1274).
inputs.net_debt_note: NARROW structural net debt (lease treatment A -- leases as debt): Bank borrowings (current 1.000 + non-current 20.722 = 21.722) + At-call deposits (28.222, third-party depositor-scheme funding) + Lease liabilities (current 2.201 + non-current 30.341 = 32.542) - Cash (10.976) = 71.510. EXCLUDES Vehicle floorplan finance (72.259) and credit contracts (0.807 net), because the FY2026 annual report states plainly (line 339-340) that 'property [is] funded by retained earnings and inventory funded by short term borrowing' -- floorplan is inventory-secured, self-liquidating financing that revolves against the vehicle inventory asset (188.428m at FY2026), not structural leverage on the going-concern business or fixed assets. This is the same narrow definition used in the prior (2026-09-24) hand-built valuation, refreshed to FY2026 actuals; total_debt here is the narrow-basis total (bank + deposits + leases) for consistency with net_debt, NOT the CSV's broad TotalDebt (154.745m, which also includes floorplan and credit contracts -- see inputs.notes for the broad figure used in the sanity check).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2026 reported FCF (OCF 85.936 - capex 5.862 = 80.074) is NOT the DCF base. It is inflated almost entirely by a one-off $53.7m inventory reduction (188.428m vs 242.162m FY2025) that will not repeat -- management explicitly frames this as a balance-sheet-strengthening exercise, not a sustainable cash-generation level. Reported FCF FY2016-26 ranged from -57.1m to +80.1m with no trend, driven by vehicle inventory/floorplan working-capital swings, not underlying trading economics (see historical_growth.notes). last_fcf instead uses a mid-cycle COMPONENT rebuild off FY2026's own EBITDA/D&A/capex (excluding the WC release): EBIT 37.554 [EBITDA 46.71 - D&A 9.156] x (1-28% tax) = NOPAT 27.039; + D&A 9.156 - capex 5.862 = 30.333. This is the reference FY0 anchor; the actual forward path is built from the component assumptions below, not compounded off this single figure.
inputs.sbc_source: Verified NIL. No share-based payment scheme disclosed in any FY2016-FY2026 filing. Explicitly zero, not missing/unavailable -- an SBC-zero NZ market per owner-fcf-adaptations.md (e). House and street bases coincide; band_position is null.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income immaterial across all periods (FY2026: $0.185m received). CMC has no material net cash pile -- it is a net-debt company -- so no strip-out is required.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A (leases as debt): lease principal is NOT deducted separately from the flows; the FY2026 D&A figure (9.156m) already includes right-of-use asset depreciation (ROU assets 29.885m at FY2026, material). Lease liabilities (32.542m) sit in the net-debt bridge instead. lease_cost_pct_path is therefore 0 in every scenario -- adding a lease charge on top of the D&A that already includes ROU depreciation would double-count.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI profit share (FY2026: 0.853m, ~4.1% of group profit before NCI) is folded into a combined leakage alongside tax via the cash_tax_rate_path: the 28% flat NZ statutory rate is applied to consolidated EBIT and no further NCI deduction is taken from the flows or the bridge, keeping the leakage small and roughly matching NCI's modest, stable ~4% share of consolidated profit (FY2025: 1.175m/~6%; FY2026: 0.853m/~4%). NCI stock itself (5.776m at FY2026) is immaterial relative to equity value and is not separately deducted in the bridge to avoid double-charging this small item.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 13.5% base WACC for an NZX small-cap, family-controlled (Gibbons >60%), thinly-traded, cyclical vehicle-dealership group. Built from an NZD risk-free rate (~4.5% 10yr NZGB) plus an equity risk premium reflecting genuine small-cap/illiquidity/cyclicality risk (~7-8pp) and modest leverage. A SINGLE WACC is used across all three scenarios (not varied by scenario) per owner-fcf-adaptations.md (f) 'charge risk once' -- cyclicality, competitive intensity (Chinese OEM entry) and the truck-cycle/agribusiness swing factors are priced directly INTO the scenario flows (revenue growth and margin paths), not stacked again as a discount-rate premium. This is a deliberate change from the prior (2026-09-24) hand-built valuation, which varied WACC 13.0/14.5/16.5% by scenario -- that charged the same cyclical/competitive risk twice (once in the bear flows, again in a higher bear WACC). See reconciliation.
inputs.notes: Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md to Owner-FCF DCF + owner-fcf-adaptations.md (non-US/cyclical/leases/NCI/SBC-zero adaptations all apply). CMC is a mature, cyclical NZ vehicle-dealership group (Ford/Mazda anchor plus Southpac trucks, Agricentre tractors, expanding BYD footprint) with a large OWNER-OCCUPIED (operational, not investment/REIT) freehold property portfolio that houses its own dealerships -- routed as an industrial/consumer cyclical with the owner-FCF engine, NOT the REIT/NAV row, because the property is used in the going-concern retail business rather than held as a separate rental-yielding investment trust. FY2026 reported FCF (80.074m) is a one-off inventory-release year (188.4m vs 242.2m inventory, -53.7m) and is NOT projectable; the component build anchors instead to a mid-cycle FY0 FCF of ~30.3m (see last_fcf note) and an EBITDA-margin path that reflects genuine, currently-declining margins (10yr range 4.29%-6.27%, FY2026 at the low end of 4.37%) rather than either the FY2022-23 COVID-inflated peak or the FY2026 trough. CEO explicitly warned (FY2026 annual report) that Chinese-OEM competitive entry has reached an 'unsustainable' level implying near-term margin pressure before an expected brand consolidation partially relieves it -- base case reflects gradual, partial margin recovery toward ~5.0-5.2% (below the FY22-23 peak), not a full reversion. Broad TotalDebt for the multiples sanity check (EV/EBITDA apples-to-apples with the historical broad-basis series) is the CSV figure 154.745m; net_debt_broad_for_sanity_check = 154.745 - 10.976 = 143.769.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blend of revenue_5yr_cagr (3.49%) and equity_10yr_cagr (6.94%), weighted toward the lower revenue figure
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGRs are negative (3yr -10.6%, 5yr -4.4%) despite positive revenue growth (3yr +2.4%, 5yr +3.5%) and positive equity growth (5yr +4.1%, 10yr +6.9%) -- a >30% divergence. This is margin compression, not a growth story: EBITDA margin fell from a FY2022-23 peak of ~6.2-6.3% to 4.37% in FY2026 as Chinese-OEM competitive entry intensified, and FY2024 EPS was additionally crushed by a one-off $12.7m non-cash deferred-tax charge (building-depreciation tax-rule change) unrelated to trading. Revenue and equity CAGRs are the more reliable growth signals here; EPS CAGR is not used as growth_rate_source because it reflects margin/tax distortion, not a genuine decline in the underlying business's growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are not meaningful and are reported as null: reported FCF (used for the raw CAGR calc were it computed) ranged from -$57.1m (FY2024) to +$80.1m (FY2026) across the 10-year history with no discernible trend, driven almost entirely by vehicle-inventory/floorplan working-capital swings rather than by growth in the underlying trading economics. A component-built mid-cycle FCF (see inputs.last_fcf) is used as the forward anchor instead of any CAGR extrapolation of the historical series.

base.narrative: Cyclical recovery continues at a moderate pace (NZ new-vehicle registrations up double digits YTD through mid-2026 before the H2 oil shock, passenger segment still +13% YoY in August 2026); revenue growth settles near its 10yr trend rate (2.1-3.5%) rather than either the FY2026 spike (+6.8%) or a renewed downturn. EBITDA margin stabilises modestly above the FY2026 trough (4.37%) as the NEV model cycle (Ranger Hybrid, Mazda 6e/CX-6e, JAC T9 PHEV, Next Gen DAF) lands through FY2027 and the BYD dealership expansion (Canterbury, Wairarapa, Taranaki) captures share CMC would otherwise cede to independent Chinese-brand networks -- but margin recovers only PART way to the FY2022-23 COVID-inflated peak (6.2-6.3%) given the CEO's own September 2026 warning that competitive intensity has reached an 'unsustainable' level that will pressure margins until brand consolidation occurs. Capex normalises from FY2026's unusually low net 0.55% of revenue (property supercycle largely complete: Fagan Motors, Avon City Ford, Southpac Palmerston North, Hutchinson Detroit Place all delivered) back toward the FY2022-25 average of ~1.6-2.2% as ongoing NEV dealership investment and ordinary asset renewal continue. Working capital remains a modest structural drag on growth (inventory/floorplan funding), not a tailwind.

bull.narrative: Chinese-OEM brand consolidation the CEO expects arrives on schedule through FY2027-28, and CMC's own BYD dealership push (Adventure Motors Canterbury/Wairarapa, Energy Motors Taranaki) is a net winner rather than a defensive hedge, capturing meaningful NEV share as weaker independent Chinese-brand entrants exit. Southpac's 'early signs' of a 2027 heavy-truck fleet-replacement recovery materialise fully once the DAF Next Generation model transition completes. Agribusiness (dairy/red meat) tailwind persists, supporting Agricentre South. Margin recovers toward and modestly through the FY2022-23 peak as scale and a rationalised competitive set restore historical trading economics, while the now-much-stronger balance sheet (FY2026 borrowings roughly a third of FY2025's level) is redeployed into further accretive property development and franchise wins (following the May-2025 Mitsubishi/Manukau and June-2026 BYD expansions).

bear.narrative: The 'unsustainable' level of Chinese-OEM competition the CEO flagged does NOT resolve via orderly consolidation -- instead it produces a prolonged margin war as more than a dozen brands fight for share in a small market, compressing EBITDA margin further below the FY2026 trough (4.37%) rather than recovering. The H2 FY2026 oil-shock demand-mix disruption (diesel/ICE-weighted inventory versus accelerating NEV demand) recurs or persists into FY2027-28 as further geopolitical/commodity shocks hit an already fragile 'slowly improving' NZ economy (management's own words). Southpac's heavy-truck 'early signs' of recovery prove premature -- the DAF model-transition 'leaner months' extend well beyond H1 FY2027 as fleet operators delay replacement capex. Ford/Ranger concentration risk crystallises as a genuine model-allocation or share-loss event (Ranger already lost the #1 spot to the Toyota RAV4 for all of calendar 2025). Thin free float and a family-controlled register mean no external catalyst forces a strategic response to the margin pressure.

scenario_narratives.base: Moderate, below-peak cyclical recovery: revenue grows near its 10yr trend rate as passenger-vehicle demand stays resilient and NEV model launches (Ranger Hybrid, Mazda 6e/CX-6e, JAC T9 PHEV, Next Gen DAF, expanding BYD footprint) offset Chinese-OEM share pressure without eliminating it; EBITDA margin recovers only partway from the FY2026 trough (4.37%) toward ~5.2%, well short of the FY2022-23 COVID-inflated peak (6.2-6.3%), reflecting the CEO's own 'unsustainable competition' warning.
scenario_narratives.bull: The CEO's expected brand consolidation arrives on schedule and CMC's BYD/NEV push is a net share winner; Southpac's truck recovery and the agribusiness tailwind both come through fully; margin recovers toward and through the FY2022-23 peak as the competitive set rationalises and the much-stronger FY2026 balance sheet funds further accretive growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: Chinese-OEM competitive intensity does not resolve via consolidation and instead produces a prolonged margin war; H2 FY2026-style demand-mix shocks recur; Southpac's truck 'early signs' prove premature and the DAF transition disruption extends; Ford/Ranger concentration risk crystallises as an actual share-loss event.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Standard 25/50/25 rather than the house 15/50/35 default. Bear weight raised from the 15% default to 25% because the CEO's own September 2026 warning of 'unsustainable' competitive intensity is an explicit, management-sourced near-term risk (not a generic macro worry), and the H2 FY2026 oil-shock episode demonstrates the group's genuine vulnerability to sudden demand-mix disruption it could not quickly adapt to. Bull weight correspondingly trimmed from the 35% default to 25% because the bull case requires several distinct things to go right simultaneously (consolidation arriving on schedule AND CMC's own BYD push winning share AND the truck cycle turning AND the agribusiness tailwind persisting) -- more conjunctive conditions than a typical bull case. Base case retained at 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Colonial Motor Company is a mature, family-controlled (Gibbons >60%), thinly-traded NZX cyclical vehicle-dealership group (Ford/Mazda anchor, Southpac heavy trucks, Agricentre tractors, an expanding BYD footprint) that also owns most of the freehold land and buildings under its own dealerships -- an owner-occupied, operational property base (not a separate rental-yielding investment trust), so this valuation routes via the owner-FCF DCF engine (industrials/cyclical row) rather than a REIT/NAV model. The single biggest judgment in this build is that FY2026's reported free cash flow ($80.1m) is a one-off: it is inflated almost entirely by a $53.7m inventory reduction (188.4m vs 242.2m) that management itself frames as balance-sheet strengthening, not a repeatable cash-generation level. The model instead anchors to a mid-cycle, component-built FY0 FCF of roughly $30.3m (EBITDA less D&A, taxed, plus D&A back, less normalised capex) and projects forward EBITDA margins that recover only partway from the FY2026 trough (4.37%, the low end of a 10-year 4.29%-6.27% range) toward roughly 5.0-5.2% in the base case -- reflecting the CEO's own explicit September 2026 warning that Chinese-OEM competitive entry has reached an 'unsustainable' level that will pressure margins until an expected brand consolidation occurs, rather than assuming a full reversion to the FY2022-23 COVID-inflated peak. A single 13.5% WACC is used across all three scenarios (cyclicality and competitive risk are priced into the scenario flows themselves, not stacked again as a discount-rate premium) and a conservative 12x terminal cap multiple in the base case keeps the terminal value close to the stock's own current ~12x trading P/E rather than assuming a re-rating. This is a deliberate change from the prior (2026-09-24) hand-built exit-P/E/exit-P/B blend, which argued the owner-FCF engine 'understates' the business; the engine's component-margin-build machinery (mid-cycle EBITDA path, working-capital capture on the revenue CHANGE rather than level) is designed for exactly this situation -- a cyclical retailer whose reported FCF is dominated by inventory swings -- and produces a more auditable, driver-by-driver result than a hand-blended multiple.
key_risks_to_valuation: Chinese-OEM competitive intensity: CEO's own 'unsustainable' warning could mean margins compress further before any consolidation relief, which would push the base case toward the bear path

Ford/Ranger concentration: ~12 of ~19+ dealerships are Ford, and any OEM allocation change or sustained share loss (Ranger already lost the #1 national spot for all of calendar 2025) hits group profitability directly
Geopolitical/commodity shocks: the H2 FY2026 Middle East oil-shock demonstrated real vulnerability to sudden demand-mix disruption the group's inventory could not quickly follow

Thin free float (Gibbons family >60%) means low liquidity and a persistent risk that the stock trades at a discount to intrinsic/property-backed value regardless of fundamentals, which the DCF cannot correct for
Southpac heavy-truck recovery is only 'early signs' per management, not confirmed data, and several leaner H1 FY2027 months are explicitly guided during the DAF model transition

Property revaluation gains (FY2026: $5.42m pre-tax through OCI) are a real source of economic value not captured in the owner-FCF flows, which value the property only through its ongoing operational contribution (capex/D&A), not its appreciation -- this valuation is therefore conservative on the property side if freehold values continue to rise

bridge.item: Prior weighted IV (exit-P/E 60% + exit-P/B 40% blend, not the owner-FCF engine)

Methodology change: switched to the owner-FCF DCF component engine per this run's explicit routing instruction, replacing the hand-built P/E/P/B blend. The prior build's OWN reference owner-FCF DCF (disclosed there as a deliberately-rejected cross-check) produced base-case IV ~$1.54 on a flat-margin, non-component basis -- this build instead uses the engine's component margin machinery (mid-cycle EBITDA path recovering from the FY2026 trough, working-capital capture on revenue CHANGE) which is designed for exactly this cyclical/WC-dominated situation and is not directly comparable to either prior figure
Anchors refreshed to FY2026 actuals: net debt roughly halved (narrow basis ~$111.0m at FY2025 vs $71.5m at FY2026, on the inventory-driven borrowings paydown), revenue +6.8%, dividend raised to 40cps

WACC de-risked from scenario-varying 13.0/14.5/16.5% to a single 13.5% across all scenarios, per the engine's 'charge risk once' rule (risk now lives in the scenario flows, not stacked in the discount rate)
New weighted IV (component owner-FCF engine, see valuation.json)
bridge.note: ties to probability_weighted.weighted_iv; not a like-for-like bridge against the prior P/E-blend figure because the valuation METHOD changed, not just the drivers -- see valuation_philosophy for the full rationale

equity_bridge.item: Property revaluation reserve (freehold land & buildings fair-value uplift over cost)
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 balance sheet, line 813: audited cumulative fair-value gain on the freehold dealership property portfolio, credited directly to equity via OCI (property revaluation reserve) and NEVER recognised in the P&L or any cash-flow line used by this DCF (trading profit, EBITDA, FCF all exclude it by IFRS construction -- fair-value movements on owner-occupied property bypass profit or loss entirely under IAS 16 revaluation model). PP&E is 49% of total assets and 83% of shareholders equity (264.982m / 320.477m) at FY2026, so this is not an immaterial add-on: the going-concern owner-FCF DCF prices only the property's ongoing OPERATING contribution (via D&A and capex in the flows) and cannot price its accumulated, independently-audited fair-value gain over cost. Added once, undiscounted, as a bridge item -- consistent with the equity_bridge contract's own example (surplus land at book) -- because it sits entirely outside the flows and so creates no double-count. This is the single most consequential judgment in this valuation: without it, the model prices CMC as if it were an asset-light dealer group, when in fact freehold ownership is a structural, explicitly-disclosed source of shareholder value (Analysis JSON moat_factors: owned freehold property, strength=strong). A conservative reader who doubts full realisability of the reserve (e.g. on a distressed or partial sale) should treat the ex-bridge operating DCF (see valuation_philosophy) as the floor case.
